assessments.reasoning: The data model classifies tuples as immutable and explains that a mutable object held by an immutable container can change value while the container continues to hold the same objects.

challenge.method: Compare appending to a list inside a tuple with replacing the tuple element.
challenge.results: Appending preserves the identity of the list in the tuple. Replacing the element would change which object the tuple holds. The passage supports that distinction.

limitations: The immutability described covers the identities contained in the tuple. Mutable referents have their own state.
The claim does not imply hashability, deep immutability or a different tuple identity.
Runtime observations use the installed CPython 3.13.5 Windows build. The documentation scope comes from the pinned 3.13.0 source.
